A szövetség szerint a kisebb kutas cégek számára nem biztosítottak a kiszámítható ellátási és gazdasági feltételek, amelyek hosszú távú működésükhöz szükségesek. Axios said that this question to Trump arose amid concerns among European leaders that Moscow might test NATO's resolve – and Trump's commitment to Article 5, the alliance's collective defense clause – through a limited attack or other military provocations, as well as in connection with CIA Director John Ratcliffe's trip to Moscow, where he met with his Russian counterpart, Sergei Naryshkin. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/slow-hors.text: Phil Harrison Fri, September 11, 2026 at 6:00 AM UTC 0 Sour and salty … Gary Oldman as Jackson Lamb in Slow Horses season six.Photograph: Jack English/Apple Pick of the week Slow Horses There are various blasts from the past as this sour and salty espionage drama returns for season six – although some have more staying power than others. In a development that might hint at a show approaching the end of its natural lifespan (although it’s been renewed for a seventh season), someone is killing former occupants of Slough House. Gary Oldman’s Jackson Lamb is typically unsentimental about this but other Horses are more concerned – particularly given the return of an old antagonist who proved to be a ruthless and relentless foe with a connection to the team. Slow Horses feels unlikely to surprise us at this point but it’s still pungently scripted and beautifully performed. Apple TV, from Wednesday 16 September *** Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story It’s an unspoken rule of fact-based fiction that the older the source material, the wilder the approach can be. This suits Ryan Murphy fine – the latest instalment of his never-knowingly-understated Monster anthology deals with Lizzie Borden (Ella Beatty), a woman who was accused of killing her father and stepmother with an axe in 1892. Borden was acquitted and lived the rest of her life in the same town, so whether she deserves to be posthumously labelled a “monster” is highly debatable. Still, various theories around the murders are tried out for lurid size. Netflix, from Thursday 17 September *** Neagley Jack Reacher’s female protege gets her own story in a drama which shares plenty of stylistic and narrative DNA with its parent show. Ex-military PI Frances Neagley (Maria Sten) is, you guessed it, a lone wolf. She’s awkward, persistent and formidable. She’s investigating the mysterious death of an old friend, which looks like a drug-related suicide but may be linked to a sinister cult. She’s battling both the police department and the cult leaders – but fortunately, she’s got some extra muscle she can call on if necessary … Prime Video, from Wednesday 16 September *** Golden Axe You’d imagine that people who are old enough to have fond memories of the 1989 Sega adventure game Golden Axe might now be too old to watch a cheesily animated version of that game. This series attempts to address that potential problem by undercutting the essential silliness of the scenario (three warriors attempt to save the land of Yuria from the giant Death Adder) with self-aware humour. It doesn’t really land: the comedy is never quite cutting enough to work as self-parody, while the plotting is too leaden to sustain much in the way of drama. Paramount+, from Wednesday 16 September *** City of Blood Set in the near future, this German drama (clunkily dubbed in English) is a pick’n’mix of modern apocalyptic scenarios. Pandemics. Economic collapse. Rampant inequality. And it’s boiling hot. Berlin is a medieval nightmare (but thankfully, banging techno seems to have survived). We see this world through the eyes of two sisters, Bea and Phoebe. Bea was adopted by a rich couple whereas Phoebe deals blood to survive. When they are reunited, they uncover a terrible secret underpinning society. It’s incoherent but the berserk relish of the world-building has appeal. Disney+, from Wednesday 16 September *** The Doll The 1890 novel by Bolesław Prus is considered to be one of Poland’s greatest ever works of fiction. It’s a love story of sorts, exploring the desire of thwarted, working-class Stanisław to move into Warsaw’s high society – which to him is represented by the beautiful, elusive, frequently scornful figure of Izabela, with whom he is obsessed. This adaptation will appeal to fans of the more pointed and polemical end of period dramas: it’s a lavish and imaginatively staged affair with an edge of darkness and danger as Stanisław spirals into paranoia. Netflix, from Wednesday 16 September *** MobLand This shonky gangland drama returns, still charmingly unaware of its own absurdity. Conrad and Maeve (Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren, chewing the scenery with real ferocity) are still nominally in charge of the Harrigan empire but a comically bloody shootout could be the catalyst for change. Meanwhile, Harry and Jan (Tom Hardy and Joanne Froggatt) are separating but their daughter Gina is establishing a criminal operation of her own. Oh, and there’s a flimsy subplot involving YouTubers which is the only indication MobLand was written this side of 1997. Log in here » LIVERPOOL – Prime Minister Mark Carney met for the first time face-to-face with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday, bonding over common values, a love of sports and a shared loss of their fathers to Alzheimer’s disease. The two leaders watched the Wolverhampton Wanderers play the Everton Football Club — Burnham’s favourite team — in a League Cup game in Liverpool, England. When they had their first call in July, a readout from 10 Downing said Burnham told Carney he “hoped to be able to roll out the blue carpet” for him in the future — a reference to Everton’s colours and the invitation to the game. Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks with High Commissioner for Canada in the United Kingdom Bill Blair, left, as he arrives in Manchester, England, on Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Justin Tang The two men sported the blue and yellow brooch of the Alzheimer Society on Wednesday, in recognition of Burham’s father who just recently died of the disease. In his own remarks, Carney noted that he too had lost his father to Alzheimer’s. Burnham called Carney a “great progressive leader” and spoke about the shared values between U.K. and Canada, and where the two have a shared opportunity on defence co-operation, trade and AI. “There’s been positive developments in that direction recently between the U.K. and Canada,” said Burnham, who took office after Keir Starmer resigned over the summer. “And it’s just so good for me to think that I will have somebody to talk to and commiserate about Everton at a G7 meeting.” Canada has formally applied to join the U.K.-led Joint Expeditionary Force as a full-time member, a bid that London is supporting, Prime Minister Mark Carney’s office said in a media statement Wednesday. The joint force is a military coalition made up of 10 allied countries focused on NATO’s northern flank. It was assembled in 2014 to create a rapid-response force. Canada’s military has worked with the force in multinational drills but has not been a permanent member of the group. In their official meeting, the two leaders talked about defence, trade and the development of artificial intelligence, according to a readout from the Prime Minister’s Office in Ottawa. It did not say whether the two leaders discussed U.S. President Donald Trump. Burnham is expected to meet Trump for the first time next week in New York. Carney’s PMO noted that the two countries are working on a “new permanent arrangement” to modernize British Army Training Unit Suffield. CFB Suffield’s 2,700-kilometre square training area in Alberta is being used by the British military for exercises and the testing of drones and other equipment. London plans to spend some $18.7 million on British Army Training Unit Suffield through to 2031. Canadian officials said London and Ottawa are also in active talks on merging their proposed defence financing initiatives to amplify their effects. A senior Canadian government official who briefed reporters on background said Ottawa is very confident they’ll reach an agreement on bringing the two proposals together to form a joint institution. Carney has championed the creation of a global Defence, Security and Resilience Bank to supply allies with low-cost borrowing for defence. Prime Minister Mark Carney, left, meets with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, England, on Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Justin Tang He’s enlisted support for that venture from eight countries, including Latvia, Luxembourg, Greece, Belgium and Ukraine. But no G7 country other than Canada has joined. The United Kingdom’s separate effort, called the Multilateral Defence Mechanism, is designed as a financing vehicle for joint purchases of military equipment and has won support from the Netherlands, Finland and Poland. British media first reported this week that Burnham’s finance minister, John Healey, is considering joining the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank. Canada and the U.K. issued a joint statement at the annual NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, this summer on how the two financial institutions could work together. The statement said the two countries want to ensure their “respective initiatives develop in a coherent and mutually supportive way” and will “seek opportunities to co-operate closely and ensure complementarity.” Money put into the defence bank counts toward the NATO target of having alliance members spend the equivalent of five per cent of their GDP on defence by 2035. The head of Canada’s Business Development Bank, Isabelle Hudon, is working as the lead negotiator for the defence bank. The U.K. is allocating $749 million toward the Multilateral Defence Mechanism and aims to stand it up in 2027.
